pages.name: Still there?
pages.task: The set's wave runs 30° ahead of the board's, as two transformers did across a paralleling switch. What fraction of the phase voltage appears across each pole?

A synchroscope dial with its pointer 40 degrees FAST, clockwise from 12. Beside it, two cycles of phase A: the board's wave solid, the set's dashed, and the thin difference across pole A. Two bars from 0 to 9 per unit, with a dashed line on the surge bar at a three-phase fault at the set. The breaker is open, so both are empty.
pages.name: The gap across a pole
pages.text: A second set runs beside a live board. Its breaker is open. Before it closes, it must match the board in four things: voltage, frequency, phase sequence and phase angle. Each pole has a board phase on one side and the set's same phase on the other. On a 440 V board each phase is 254 V. What the pole sees is the difference between them. That is the voltage across the pole. The set's wave runs 40° ahead. So the pole sees 2 sin 20° × 254 = 174 V.

pages.alt: The live board's three busbars, A, B and C, run down through the breaker, now open, to the incoming set. Across the poles, lamp A is bright, lamp B is bright and lamp C is bright. A synchroscope dial with its pointer 60 degrees FAST, clockwise from 12. Beside it, two cycles of phase A: the board's wave solid, the set's dashed, and the thin difference across pole A. Two bars from 0 to 9 per unit, with a dashed line on the surge bar at a three-phase fault at the set. The breaker is open, so both are empty.
pages.name: Sixty degrees
pages.task: The set's wave runs 60° ahead of the board's. Each phase is 254 V. What voltage appears across each pole?
pages.why: 2 × sin 30° × 254 = 2 × 0.5 × 254 = 254 V. That is a whole phase voltage.

pages.alt: The live board's three busbars, A, B and C, run down through the breaker, now open, to the incoming set. Across the poles, lamp A is bright, lamp B is bright and lamp C is bright. A synchroscope dial with its pointer 60 degrees FAST, clockwise from 12. Beside it, two cycles of phase A: the board's wave solid, the set's dashed, and the thin difference across pole A. Two bars from 0 to 9 per unit, with a dashed line on the surge bar at a three-phase fault at the set. The breaker is open, so both are empty.
pages.name: Slip
pages.text: Now the set runs 0.2 Hz faster than the board. That frequency difference is the slip. The set's waves gain one whole cycle every 1 ÷ 0.2 = 5 s. So the angle creeps round, and the gap swells and shrinks every 5 s. The three lamps glow and go dark together. The dial is a synchroscope. Its pointer turns once each slip cycle. It turns clockwise when the set runs fast. It stands at 12 when the angle is zero.

pages.alt: The live board's three busbars, A, B and C, run down through the breaker, now open, to the incoming set. Across the poles, lamp A is dark, lamp B is dark and lamp C is dark. A synchroscope dial with its pointer at 12, in phase. Beside it, two cycles of phase A: the board's wave solid, the set's dashed, and the thin difference across pole A. Two bars from 0 to 9 per unit, with a dashed line on the surge bar at a three-phase fault at the set. The breaker is open, so both are empty.
pages.name: One turn
pages.task: The set runs at 60.25 Hz on a 60 Hz board. How long does the pointer take to go once round?
pages.why: The slip is 60.25 − 60 = 0.25 Hz. The set gains a quarter of a cycle each second. So a whole cycle takes 1 ÷ 0.25 = 4 s.

pages.alt: The live board's three busbars, A, B and C, run down through the breaker, now shut, to the incoming set. The lamps across the poles are dark, shorted by the shut breaker. A synchroscope dial with its pointer at 12, in phase. A ring marks where Close went and a dot where the breaker shut at 90° FAST. Beside it, two cycles of phase A: the board's wave solid, the set's dashed and lying on it. Two bars from 0 to 9 per unit, with a dashed line on the surge bar at a three-phase fault at the set. Surge 5.7 per unit, shaft torque 4.0 per unit, both red: the close was outside the window.
pages.name: A close out of step
pages.text: Suppose the breaker shuts a quarter turn out. Shut at 90°, each pole sees 359 V. The reactances of the set and the board are the main limit on the surge that gap drives. Here it is 5.7 per unit. The surge also yanks the rotor into step. That puts 4.0 per unit of torque through the shaft and coupling. Shut at 180° and the surge reaches 8.0 per unit. That is more than a three-phase fault at the set.

pages.alt: The live board's three busbars, A, B and C, run down through the breaker, now open, to the incoming set. Across the poles, lamp A is dark, lamp B is dark and lamp C is dark. A synchroscope dial with its pointer at 12, in phase. Beside it, two cycles of phase A: the board's wave solid, the set's dashed, and the thin difference across pole A. Two bars from 0 to 9 per unit, with a dashed line on the surge bar at a three-phase fault at the set. The breaker is open, so both are empty.
pages.answer: No, each pole sees about twice the phase voltage
pages.name: Bottom of the dial
options: No, each pole sees about twice the phase voltage
pages.task: Both voltmeters read 440 V. The pointer is at the bottom of the dial, at 180°. It is turning slowly. Can you close?
pages.why: At 180° the waves are opposite. Each pole sees 2 × sin 90° × 254 = 508 V. That gives the biggest surge of all. Wait for the pointer to come round to 12.

pages.alt: The live board's three busbars, A, B and C, run down through the breaker, now shut, to the incoming set. The lamps across the poles are dark, shorted by the shut breaker. A synchroscope dial with its pointer at 12, in phase. A ring marks where Close went and a dot where the breaker shut at 12. A faded dot marks the first close, which shut at 3.6° FAST. Beside it, two cycles of phase A: the board's wave solid, the set's dashed and lying on it. Two bars from 0 to 9 per unit, with a dashed line on the surge bar at a three-phase fault at the set. Surge 0.0 per unit, shaft torque 0.0 per unit, both small.
pages.name: The advance angle
pages.text: A breaker takes a set time to shut after the command. Say 50 ms. At 0.2 Hz slip the pointer turns 360 × 0.2 = 72° a second. In 50 ms it moves 72 × 0.05 = 3.6°. So if you press Close at 12, the breaker shuts 3.6° past it. Instead, send the close 3.6° before 12. That lead is the advance angle. The dial shows both. The first close lands 3.6° past 12. The second, sent 3.6° early, lands at 12.

pages.alt: The live board's three busbars, A, B and C, run down through the breaker, now shut, to the incoming set. The lamps across the poles are dark, shorted by the shut breaker. A synchroscope dial with its pointer at 12, in phase. A ring marks where Close went and a dot where the breaker shut at 9° FAST. Beside it, two cycles of phase A: the board's wave solid, the set's dashed and lying on it. Two bars from 0 to 9 per unit, with a dashed line on the surge bar at a three-phase fault at the set. Surge 0.6 per unit, shaft torque 0.6 per unit, both edged red and marked Outside the window.
pages.name: Late by
pages.task: The set runs 0.5 Hz fast. The breaker takes 50 ms. You press Close just as the pointer passes 12. How many degrees past 12 does the breaker shut?
pages.why: 360 × 0.5 = 180° a second. 180 × 0.05 = 9°. Pressing at 12 lands 9° late. So the close should go 9° early.

pages.alt: The live board's three busbars, A, B and C, run down through the breaker, now open, to the incoming set, whose B and C leads are swapped. Across the poles, lamp A is dark, lamp B is blazing and lamp C is blazing. A synchroscope dial with its pointer at 12, in phase. Beside it, two cycles of phase A: the board's wave solid, the set's dashed, and the thin difference across pole A. Two bars from 0 to 9 per unit, with a dashed line on the surge bar at a three-phase fault at the set. The breaker is open, so both are empty.
pages.name: Phase sequence
pages.text: Two of the set's phases, B and C, are now swapped. The lamps no longer dim together. One goes dark while the other two blaze. The dark lamp runs round the three in turn. When lamp A is dark, lamps B and C each see 440 V. The pointer turns exactly as before. It compares only phase A on each side. So it cannot see the order of the other two. The wiring fixes the phase sequence. It is the phase rotation you already test.

pages.alt: The live board's three busbars, A, B and C, run down through the breaker, now shut, to the incoming set, whose B and C leads are swapped. The lamps across the poles are dark, shorted by the shut breaker. A synchroscope dial with its pointer at 12, in phase. A ring marks where Close went and a dot where the breaker shut at 12. Surge 6.9 per unit, shaft torque Wrong sequence, both red: the close was outside the window.
pages.answer: No, the phase sequence is wrong
pages.name: Crossed phases
options: Yes, the pointer is at 12 and turning slowly
No, the phase sequence is wrong
No, wait until all three lamps are bright
pages.task: The pointer turns slowly through 12. Lamp A is dark, but lamps B and C are bright. Can you close?
pages.why: With the sequence right, all three lamps go dark together. Here B and C blaze at 440 V while A is dark. So B and C are crossed. Put the wiring right first.

pages.name: The relay
pages.text: With a relay in charge, Close only asks. The relay closes only inside its window. Here it is 10°, 0.2 Hz and 2% of voltage. Makers set it anywhere from 0.5% to 5% on voltage and 0.1 to 0.5 Hz on slip. At 0.5 Hz slip it refuses and says why. At 60.10 Hz it agrees. It waits for the advance angle, 1.8°, and sends the close. The breaker shuts at 12. An automatic synchroniser also trims the governor and the AVR, by moving their set points.

pages.alt: The live board's three busbars, A, B and C, run down through the breaker, now open, to the incoming set. Across the poles, lamp A is dim, lamp B is dim and lamp C is dim. A synchroscope dial with its pointer 29 degrees SLOW, anticlockwise from 12. Beside it, two cycles of phase A: the board's wave solid, the set's dashed, and the thin difference across pole A. Two bars from 0 to 9 per unit, with a dashed line on the surge bar at a three-phase fault at the set. The breaker is open, so both are empty.
pages.answer: Raise the field, and lower the fuel a little
pages.name: Trim before closing
options: Raise the field, and lower the fuel a little
Raise the fuel, and lower the field a little
Raise the field only, then close as the pointer passes 12
pages.task: The set reads 420 V and 60.40 Hz. The board is 440 V, 60 Hz. What do you trim before closing?
pages.why: More field raises the voltage towards 440 V. Less fuel slows the set until the pointer turns slowly enough to catch at 12.

pages.name: Advance for 80 ms
pages.task: A relay must shut a breaker at 12. The set runs 0.3 Hz fast. The breaker takes 80 ms. How many degrees before 12 does the relay send the close? Give it to one decimal place.
pages.why: 360 × 0.3 = 108° a second. 108 × 0.08 = 8.64°. To one decimal place that is 8.6°.
